comment: Book-study loop queue (librarian lane of the scholar loop). One unit = one book theme studied deeply. HONESTY RULE: Bob does not have the copyrighted texts; the librarian studies each book's ideas through public materials — author talks, essays, podcasts (e.g. Engelstein's Ludology), interviews, published excerpts, detailed reviews, BGG threads — and records the FRAMEWORKS with attribution, never reproducing text. If a book's depth clearly exceeds what public materials give, the unit's card ends with a one-line purchase recommendation for the owner. Multi-unit books get one unit per major theme.

units.book: Everybody Wins — James Wallis
units.topic: Four decades of Spiel des Jahres winners: what the jury rewarded era by era, and which winners still get played (survival vs award)

units.book: GameTek — Geoff Engelstein
units.topic: Probability + psychology essays: loss aversion at the table, the mathematics of catch-up, randomness perception (input vs output luck)

units.book: GameTek — Geoff Engelstein
units.topic: Game science applied: auction theory, tension curves, cognitive load limits — extract every quantifiable design dial

units.book: Building Blocks of Tabletop Game Design — Engelstein & Shalev
units.topic: The mechanics encyclopedia: full taxonomy structure (categories, ~200 mechanisms), which mechanisms combine well and which collide — map onto Bob's DIRECTIONS arms

units.book: A Theory of Fun — Raph Koster
units.topic: Fun = learning: pattern mastery, why games get boring (the grok point), what this implies for a game meant to survive 10 plays

units.book: Characteristics of Games — Elias, Garfield & Gutschera
units.topic: The core traits framework: game length, player count effects, heuristics ladder, kingmaking, orthogame vs metagame — Bob's evaluator vocabulary

units.book: Characteristics of Games — Elias, Garfield & Gutschera
units.topic: Luck vs skill formally: how they define and measure it; the skill-band problem (a game must be winnable by the weaker player often enough)

units.book: Around the World in Eighty Games — Marcus du Sautoy
units.topic: The mathematical tour: which mathematical structures (combinatorics, topology, probability) hide inside beloved games; math as a novelty source

units.book: Board Games in 100 Moves — Livingstone & Wallis
units.topic: Milestone map of 5,000 years: the inflection points where a new physical component (dice, cards, standees, apps) created a new genre — precedent for 3D print as the next component revolution

units.book: The Oxford History of Board Games — David Parlett
units.topic: The deep taxonomy of traditional games (race, space, chase, displace, deploy) and what centuries of folk iteration converged on

units.book: Uncertainty in Games — Greg Costikyan
units.topic: The eleven sources of uncertainty; matching uncertainty type to audience; hidden info vs randomness vs performative uncertainty — a checklist for Bob's ideator

units.book: The Art of Game Design — Jesse Schell
units.topic: The lenses relevant to tabletop: essential experience, surprise, fun, balance, and the playtesting chapters — convert applicable lenses into Bob review-agent prompts

units.book: Clockwork Game Design — Keith Burgun
units.topic: The single-core-mechanism discipline: build one clockwork around one decision, strip everything else — the strongest argument for Bob's minimal-ruleset bias

units.book: Kobold Guide to Board Game Design — Selinker, Garfield, Ernest, et al.
units.topic: Working designers' essays: prototyping speed, development vs design, publisher lessons — the craft habits Bob's pipeline should mirror

units.book: Rules of Play — Salen & Zimmerman
units.topic: Meaningful play + rules as systems: discernible/integrated outcomes — the formal test for whether a Bob decision matters

units.book: Playing at the World — Jon Peterson
units.topic: How wargames became D&D: hobby-community dynamics, why some innovations spread — distribution lessons for a new-genre inventor

units.book: Seven Games — Oliver Roeder
units.topic: What computers did to checkers/chess/go/poker/scrabble/bridge/backgammon — solved-game risk, and what stays fun after machines win; directly informs Bob's dominant-strategy gate

units.book: Gamish: A Graphic History of Gaming — Edward Ross
units.topic: Cross-cultural play impulse: what every culture independently invented — the universals Bob can rely on

units.book: Ludology podcast corpus — Engelstein & Shalev (public)
units.topic: Mine the public episode index for design-theory episodes that extend GameTek/Building Blocks; card the top 10 lessons with episode citations

units.book: Mark Rosewater corpus (public GDC talks + Drive to Work)
units.topic: 'Twenty Years, Twenty Lessons' in full + restrictions breed creativity — convert into Bob ideator constraints
